entities.name: Alliance Party of Northern Ireland
entities.label: Institution
entities.summary:
The Alliance Party of Northern Ireland, founded in 1970 as a cross-community party explicitly bridging Northern Ireland's Protestant-unionist and Catholic-nationalist divide, is the only significant political party in Northern Ireland that is neither unionist nor nationalist — instead advocating for a 'shared future' that transcends sectarian division — and has experienced dramatic growth since the 2022 Northern Ireland Assembly elections, becoming the third-largest party and signaling a significant shift in Northern Irish politics away from its traditional sectarian two-bloc structure.

Alliance was founded by Phelim O'Neill, Anne Dickson, and others in the months before the Northern Ireland Troubles escalated into full-scale violence, embodying the hope that cross-community moderate politics could prevent the coming conflict. Through 50 years of violence, political deadlock, and sectarian polarization, Alliance maintained its cross-community stance while remaining relatively small. The 2016 Brexit referendum — which Northern Ireland voted 56% to Remain — transformed Alliance's position: its pro-European, cross-community stance resonated with a younger generation disillusioned with traditional unionist/nationalist politics.

The 2022 Stormont Assembly elections saw Sinn Féin emerge as the largest party (historic), the DUP as second, and Alliance as third with 17 seats — its best ever result. Alliance leader Naomi Long became the first Alliance politician to serve as First Minister-designate for any period. The party's growth reflects a broader shift in Northern Irish society toward a 'neither' identity — identifying as 'Northern Irish' rather than British or Irish — particularly among young voters in Belfast and other urban areas.

historicalSignificance.significanceNarrative: Alliance Party of Northern Ireland — maintaining cross-community politics through 50 years of sectarian conflict, growing dramatically in the post-Brexit era, and representing a possible future beyond Northern Ireland's unionist-nationalist binary — is one of the most historically significant small parties in UK politics.
